item.title: [100] Yes, Americans not caring about soccer that much is legitimate.
item.description:
Let's stop and use our brains for a moment.
The USA has 4 other major sports and several Olympic events they dominate in. Their best talent and resources are going towards all of that.
Association Football, while popular, is on the niche side. And due to how worldwide the sport is, the countries that care the most do the best. Look at all the world cup winners. They have their niche sports but its overwhelmingly football.
Despite not caring as much, we still make the world cup and reach the Knockout stage which you have to admit is impressive.
When will Americans genuinely start taking the sport seriously? I don't know, it's up to them. But the potential IS there. We just...don't care much. Lol
Thoughts? I feel like i've been hearing "soccer is growing in the USA!" for the past 2 decades but i think it is for sure now. I do want us to start caring.

item.title: [ 91] MLS is Sleeping Giant
item.description:
MLS is serious threat to European soccer. Sure right now its easy to poke fun at them but if you look at it from an analytical perspective.

>MLS has had consistent steady growth for 3 decades and is reaching a big tipping point where growth dramatically accelerates
>MLS already more popular than NHL, its only behind NFL,NBA,MLB in popularity.
>30 teams now
>growing fan bases year over year
>stable finances
>Powerful ownership groups
>Apple TV+ actually believes in them and removed them from pay wall recently. Now anyone with 4.99 Apple sub can see every MLS game globally, anywhere.
>Teams all building proper soccer specific stadiums
>MLS starting to recruit harder in Latin America
>World cup viewership proving that theirs an appetite for Soccer in U.S
>30 Million saw U.S vs Belgium game, all games performed well consistently
>Mexico games also got over 15 million views consistently
>Disney out of nowhere wants world cup rights now, will probably bitch slap Fox and take them easily.
>Disney will probably steal MLS rights from Apple TV
>The Mouse gets what it wants
>Needs subs for its ESPN streaming service, will invest heavily in sport
>In 2030's you will see MLS aggressively go after top Euro talent
>You will have to sign up for ESPN streaming to see your Sir Duncan Footie score goals for LAFC in front of sold out Mexican crowds.
> Mexico sees this and wants in theirs persistent rumors that Liga MX wants to full merge with MLS to form Mega league. Of course wont happen but just shows how hungry they are to grow
>They all see Mickey Mouse with money bag getting ready to move in.
>Expect significant growth to MLS by 2030's, which includes good Euro talent being taken to MLS.

TLDR: MLS is well positioned for massive growth in near future and powerful media companies like Disney all of sudden care about soccer. They will pump in more money and you will see better talent in MLS.

All aspects of a Pokémon are customizable with VP, a currency earned simply by playing the game. IVs are also removed.

US$6.99 one time purchase for 50 training tickets (fully train for free), 30 Teammate Tickets (recruit Pokemon without using VP), 50 extra box space and the LGPE trainer music. Only available on Switch for now.

>I want to learn the game, where do I begin?
Download PTCGL at https://tcg.pokemon.com/en-us/tcgl
The game has a quick tutorial and a bunch of decent decks to get you started against other beginners or against the AI. Some of those decks are very close to meta too. You can also go to your local game store and see if people are playing Pokémon.

You have a decent beginner's guide at https://www.justinbasil.com/guide
There's also the old /tcg/ guide at https://imgur.com/a/W4NkOu6
After that, look up meta decks and try to reverse engineer them to see how things work.

Donald Trump’s latest effort to delay the release of more than $5m in court-held funds that he owes E Jean Carroll failed on Wednesday.

The US president asked Manhattan federal court judge Lewis Kaplan late on Tuesday not to order the release of these court-held funds, which a jury awarded Carroll in her successful 2023 sexual abuse and defamation civil trial against him; this money also includes interest. Trump has denied all wrongdoing.

Less than 24 hours later, Kaplan issued an order directing the disbursement of this money. Within an hour, Trump filed paperwork indicating that he is appealing this decision.

“The Clerk is respectfully directed to disburse … the value of the principle Judgment, which amounts to $5,000,000.00,” Kaplan’s order said. “The Clerk is further respectfully directed to disburse … the value of the post-judgment interest”.

Trump had deposited this multimillion jury award, plus 11% interest, into a court-controlled account about six weeks after Carroll’s win. For this money, which now totals about $5.8m, to be released, Kaplan had to order directing the court-controlled fund to do so.

Trump’s failed request stems from the supreme court’s 29 June decision not to review his appeal of this case. Trump had asked for the supreme court to weigh his appeal after lower courts repeatedly rejected his fight against this verdict.

After the supreme court denied hearing his appeal, Carroll’s legal team asked Manhattan federal court judge Lewis Kaplan to issue an order directing the release of these funds.

item.title: [205] VOO and Chill
item.description:
The more I look into investing and compare the historical returns of certain ETFs / individual stocks it seems like the whole philosophy of “VOO and Chill” is equal parts really smart and retarded
It’s like a no brainer for money but even now as long as the market is in a growth period shouldn’t you at least do QQQ?
It seems so simple that’d you miss a lot of upside but the returns are honestly not bad and extremely consistent
How accurate is this assessment? It’s both so simple and guaranteed that everyone should it but also too safe so you end up missing out on more upside
I’m talking 5-20 years investing here not trading
